THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 28.10.2017 PASSED IN MVC NO.998/2012 ON THE FILE OF THE XXII ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSES JUDGE AND XX A.C.M.M. AND MEMBER M.A.C.T.,
BENGALURU, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR HEARING THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The appellant who is the petitioner in MVC No.998/2012 before the learned XXII Additional Small Causes and XX ACMM and MACT, Bengaluru, is assailing the judgment and award on the ground of quantum of compensation.
2. The brief facts are as below:

On 16.06.2011 at about 6.45 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding in a Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-N-6819 on Bengaluru to Chennai, when the petitioner reached near Sikkarimedu Bus Stop, at that time the said Car driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the front foot board of the bus bearing Reg.No.TN-29-N-1508.

Due to which, the NC:
2023:KHC:21113 petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital, Krishnagiri for first aid treatment, thereafter he was shifted to Suguna Hospital, Bengaluru for further treatment and admitted as an inpatient from 16.06.2011 to 23.06.2011.
Petitioner claims that he has sustained comminuted fracture of right acetabulum, fracture of 5th rib of right side and other injuries.

The petitioner underwent operations for acetabulum, plates and screws were inserted and he was discharged and spent `4,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food and nourishment and he has to undergo one more operation for removal of implants incurring future medical expenses.

The Petitioner contended that, at the time of accident he was working as a Technical Director at MICROCON i2i Private Ltd., Bommasandra Industrial Area,
Bengaluru on a monthly salary of `70,000/- and due to accidental injuries, he is unable to perform his duties.

Further submitted that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the Car bearing NC: 2023:KHC:21113 Reg.No.KA-51-N-6819 by its driver and the Kurubarapalli Police have registered a case in Crime No. 242/2011 under Section 279, 337 of IPC.
The 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the said Car are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation with interest.
3. On issuance of notice, respondent Nos. 1 and 2 before the Tribunal and respondent No.2 filed the objections and respondent No.1 had not filed any objections.

Sri. Vijay Kumar G. H vs M/S. Microcon I2I Pvt Ltd on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59386133/
2 4.

entities.text: Vijay Kumar G. H vs M/S. Microcon I2I Pvt Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 contended that the owner and insurer of the bus are necessary parties and denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed was termed to be highly exorbitant, imaginary and untenable in law.

It has contended that the terms and conditions of the police were violated by the driver of the car and therefore, the liability has to be fastened upon respondent No.1-owner.
5.
The Tribunal on the basis of the above pleadings, framed necessary issues and petitioner was examined as NC: 2023:KHC:21113 PW1 and Exs.P1 to P17
were marked and two witnesses were examined on his behalf as PWs 2 and 3.
On behalf of respondent No.1, its official has been examined as RW1 and Ex.R1 was marked.

6. After hearing the arguments, the Tribunal awarded a sum of `1,76,400/- under different heads,
directing the respondent No.2 insurance company to pay the same along with interest.
7. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioner is before this Court in appeal.

8. On issuance of the notice, respondent No.2 insurance company has appeared before this Court through its counsel and notice to respondent No.1 was served, he did not appear before this Court.
9.
On admitting the appeal, the Tribunal records have been secured and the arguments by both the sides were heard.

10. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submit that the petitioner though was earning `70,000/- per month and such income of the petitioner was proved NC: 2023:KHC:21113 through the PW3, the Tribunal erred in holding that such income is not proved and therefore, adopted the notional income of `10,000/- per month.
He further contends that the compensation awarded under the other heads of the compensation are also abysmally low.
He contended that Tribunal also erred in coming to the conclusion that the petitioner has not lost his job and therefore, he was not entitled for compensation under he head of loss of future income.

11. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 Insurance Company contended that the Tribunal is justified in holding the notional income of the petitioner at `10,000/- per month and that the Tribunal has rightly assessed the evidence on record that the petitioner has not suffered any financial disability as he has continued in the service and as such no interference is required in the impugned judgment.

12. A perusal of the impugned judgment and the records available was that the petitioner had produced Ex.P11 salary certificate which shows that he was earning NC: 2023:KHC:21113 `70,000/-
per month in support of his contention, he examined the PW3 who is a Marketing Manager of the respondent No.1- Company.
In his evidence, he has stated that he do not know about the details of the salary and it is maintained by the Accounts Department and he had not seen any records in respect of the same.
He admits that, he is not the owner of the company.
He also admits that the Accounts Department is not related to him.
In view of the said evidence of PW3, it can be safely be said that PW3 is not having any knowledge about the details of the salary and he only issued Ex.P11.

Sri. Vijay Kumar G. H vs M/S. Microcon I2I Pvt Ltd on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59386133/
3

entities.text: Vijay Kumar G. H vs M/S. Microcon I2I Pvt Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, it is difficulty to accept that the petitioner was earning `70,000/- per month as claimed by him.
13. The petitioner has produced the IT returns for the financial year 2009 and 2011.
This income tax returns show that there was a TDS to the extent of `4,000/- per month and the declared income of the petitioner was `6,30,365/-.
However, this income tax returns is not marked and no reasons are available in the Tribunal record as to why it was marked not.

However, it is NC: 2023:KHC:21113 relevant to note that Ex.P11 salary certificate also mentions about the TDS deduction at `5,000/- per month and the salary in respect of May 2011 and therefore, on a careful perusal of the evidence available on record, it can be safely be said that petitioner was earning `50,000/- per month after deduction of taxes and other cess.
14.
The evidence of PWs 1 and 3 show that the petitioner has not continued in the job as Technical Director.
Thus, discontinuation of the job of the petitioner cannot be attributed to the injuries suffered by him.
There is no mention either in the evidence of PW1 or PW3 that due to the accidental injuries suffered by him he was incapacitated from continuing his job as Technical director.
The fracture of right acetabulum cannot be sufficient enough to held that a Technical Director in a company could lose his job.
Therefore, in the absence of any documentary evidence either by PW1 or PW3, it is to be held that the petitioner has continued in the said job.
15. In the result, the petitioner is not entitled for a compensation under the head of 'future loss of income'.
It NC: 2023:KHC:21113 is already noted that the petitioner has suffered fracture of right acetabulum and fracture of right 5th rib.
Though PW2 has stated that it has resulted in a disability of 20% and it has not affected the future earning capacity.
Under these circumstances, the Tribunal was justified in rejecting the claim for future loss of income.
16. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `25,000/- under the head of 'pain and sufferings' as the fracture of right acetabulum and the fracture of the 5th rib are grievous injuries and
apart from that,
he had suffered abrasion over chin and the face.
Therefore, the compensation of `25,000/- awarded under the head of pain and suffering appears to be inadequate.
Hence, the same is enhanced to `45,000/-.
17. The compensation awarded under the head of 'medical expenses' is based on the bills produced and therefore, it do not require any enhancement.
18. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `20,000/- under the head of food and nourishment expenses, conveyance and attendant charges.
The petitioner was - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:21113 inpatient for 8 days an therefore, the compensation of `20,000/- is adequate and no enhancement is permissible.

Sri. Vijay Kumar G. H vs M/S. Microcon I2I Pvt Ltd on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59386133/
4 19.

entities.text: Vijay Kumar G. H vs M/S. Microcon I2I Pvt Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `30,000/- under the head of 'loss of income during the laid up period'.

It is relevant to note that the fracture of right acetebulum and the fracture of 5th rib were treated with ORIF and therefore, it can be safely be said that he was unable to resume his work atleast for a period of two months.

Hence, loss of income during the laid up period is calculated as `1,00,000/- (`50,000 x 2).
20.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `75,000/- under the head of 'loss of amenities in life'.
This quantum of compensation was in the light of the fact that the petitioner was not entitled for loss of future income.
Hence, the said compensation is adequate.

21. In view of the above discussion, the petitioner is entitled for additional compensation of `90,000/- (`20,000/- towards pain and suffering and `70,000/- towards loss of income during treatment period) with - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:21113 interest in addition to what has been awarded by the tribunal.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified by awarding a sum of `90,000/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its depot.
(iii) The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks.
(iv) The rest of the conditions imposed by the Tribunal are unaltered.
Learned counsel for respondent is permitted to file vakalath within four weeks.
